clue.text: Coming up with rude hairstyle, "Airhole"

indicators.note: in a down clue, up asks for the hairstyle's letters to be read from the bottom

parts.note: a DA, or duck's arse, is a slicked-back quiff with a vulgar name
a vent is an opening that lets air through

explanation.surface: A coming-up-with of a cheeky haircut with a breathing hole in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A DA, or duck's arse, is a 1950s greaser haircut named for its rear-end shape, hence 'rude'.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means an arrival or coming, especially of something awaited.

clue.text: Measure beer and turn resentful

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of measure
bitter is a British style of hoppy draught beer

explanation.surface: Someone measures out their beer and grows sour about it.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is a British pub beer, amber and well hopped.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter someone is to make them sour and aggrieved, so it is a verb of turning resentful.

clue.text: Prince has "Fever" for a 6

parts.note: ague is an old word for a malarial fever with shivering

explanation.surface: A royal comes down with a fever and is replaced by an orchestral piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 refers to the answer at 6-down: the themed answers are named symphonies; this is Mozart's No 38.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Symphony No 38 is nicknamed after the Czech capital, making it one such orchestral work.

clue.text: Violins lacking depth without American composer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shortened violins go round the American
lacking tells us the depth letter is dropped from the violins

parts.note: Strads are Stradivarius violins
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: Violins with no depth, minus an American, make a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Strads are violins made by Antonio Stradivari; 'without' here is the old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss (and the Viennese waltz family of that name) are famous composers.

clue.text: Salon do, not including a 6

indicators.note: including signals that the run of letters sits within the words before it

explanation.surface: A salon party that excludes something, in mock gossip-column style.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans salON DO Not, ignoring the comma. Haydn's last symphony, No 104, carries this nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's Symphony No 104 is known by the name of the British capital, one of the themed orchestral works.

clue.text: Alastair, reportedly, wants counterfeit work on a big scale

indicators.note: reportedly means the surname is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Alastair Sim was a British comic film actor
phony means fake or counterfeit

explanation.surface: Someone named Alastair supposedly wants a fake piece of large-scale work.
explanation.walkthrough: Alastair Sim, star of the St Trinian's films, gives a sound SYM.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is an extended orchestral composition, a musical work on a grand scale.

clue.text: Not a sensible judge's outline

parts.note: a person who is not a sensible one is a dumb one, giving the phrase a dumb
to judge is to rate or assess

explanation.surface: A judge who is not sensible gives an outline of the case.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'Not a sensible' is read as 'a dumb'; the 's of judge's is part of that piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to sketch or give a faint outline of something.

clue.text: Could be an octopus put heartlessly in the drink

indicators.note: in places the shortened word within the drink

parts.note: pop is a fizzy soft drink

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the middle letter of the word for put

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: An octopus might be put, without much care, into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Polyp once meant an octopus, from Greek for many-footed, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyp was once a name for an octopus or cuttlefish, from Greek for many-footed, so an octopus could be one.

clue.text: Reginald Perrin's last outing gets a 6

indicators.note: an outing takes the letters on a trip, rearranging them
last picks the final letter of the surname

explanation.surface: Reginald Perrin finally goes on an outing and is rewarded with a symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Reginald Perrin is the hero of a British TV sitcom about a man who fakes his own death. Shostakovich's Seventh carries this city name.
explanation.definitionFit: Shostakovich's Symphony No 7 is named after the besieged Russian city, a themed orchestral work.

clue.text: Drug City's without drug (not "E")

indicators.note: without in its sense of outside, so the city goes round the trimmed drug

parts.note: LA is short for Los Angeles

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the named letter from the second drug

parts.note: dope is slang for an illicit drug
E is given in quotes as the letter itself

explanation.surface: A city goes without a drug, but specifically not ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside; L-dopa is a Parkinson's treatment, so 'Drug' and 'drug' play different roles.
explanation.definitionFit: L-dopa is a medical drug used to treat Parkinson's disease.

clue.text: A 6 — no bull!

definitions.meaning: Haydn's Symphony No 82 is nicknamed for an animal, one of the themed works
on the stock market a bull expects rises; its opposite expects falls

explanation.walkthrough: Haydn's Symphony No 82 is the one nicknamed after this animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear is a market pessimist, the opposite of a bull; also Haydn's symphony nickname.

clue.text: Law suit finally disposed of — for a figure

indicators.note: disposed of means a letter of the law is thrown away

parts.note: a statute is a written law

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word suit

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is finally settled, all over a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of suit, T, is removed from STATUTE. 'Law suit' looks like a lawsuit but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure.

clue.text: Antelope's second youth of secondary importance? Yes

parts.note: a teen is a young person
B grade, or B-list, means second rank
OK means yes

explanation.surface: Is an antelope's second youngster of lesser importance? Yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Antelope is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The steenbok is a small southern African antelope.

clue.text: Rod, suitably marked, might serve thus on most occasions

definitions.text: Rod, suitably marked, might serve thus
definitions.meaning: a rod with marks along it could be used as a measuring stick

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'as a ruler' minus its last letter: a marked rod might serve in that way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means generally or usually, true on most occasions.

clue.text: "Teacher is nosy", said a 6

indicators.note: said means the phrase is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: sir is what pupils call a male teacher; being nosy he pries

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the teacher is nosy, and calls it a symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR PRIES spoken sounds like the answer. Haydn's Symphony No 94 has a sudden loud chord giving its nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's Symphony No 94 is named for its unexpected fortissimo chord, one of the themed works.

clue.text: Zero over zero equals a 6

indicators.note: in a down clue, over asks for the word to be turned upwards

parts.note: nil means zero
z is used for zero, as in the Z axis's origin

explanation.surface: A mock equation: zero divided by zero equals a symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's Symphony No 36 is named after this Austrian city; 'over' in a down clue means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Symphony No 36 was written in and named after this Austrian city, a themed orchestral work.

clue.text: Desert islander's casual dress occasions?

definitions.meaning: Man Friday is Robinson Crusoe's companion on the desert island, so this is his possessive
many offices allow dress-down days at the end of the week

explanation.definitionFit: Dress-down days are traditionally the last working day of the week, and Crusoe's companion was Friday.

clue.text: A 6 setter into disco dancing round the Junction

indicators.note: round means the built word goes round the junction letter
into places the setter within the rearranged disco
dancing jumbles the letters of disco

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a T-junction is where one road meets another at a right angle

explanation.surface: A symphony composer pushes into a disco and dances round a junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' makes DOSIC from disco; 'into' puts ME inside to give DOMESIC; 'round' wraps that round T. This is Strauss's Sinfonia Domestica.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss's Sinfonia Domestica is a programme symphony about family life, one of the themed works.

clue.text: Hands that are all over the place?

definitions.text: Hands that are all over the place?

parts.words: Hands that are all over the place?
parts.note: hand here means handwriting, untidy and sprawling across the page

explanation.definitionFit: Untidy handwriting is called scrawl, so messy hands in the handwriting sense are these.

clue.text: Prepare "Silver" — is able to back "Spirit"

parts.note: to arm is to prepare for battle
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: back means the word for is able is reversed

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: Get Silver ready, the horse that can back a spirited rider.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN read backwards gives NAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a French grape brandy, a spirit like cognac.

clue.text: Like a totally traditional Swedish kitchen left out for a 6

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is removed

parts.words: Like a totally traditional Swedish kitchen
parts.note: an old Scandinavian kitchen is made entirely of pine wood, so all pine

explanation.surface: A traditional Swedish kitchen, all pine, is passed over for a symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL PINE minus one L gives the answer. This is Richard Strauss's Alpine Symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss's Eine Alpensinfonie depicts a mountain climb, one of the themed works.

clue.text: Note embedded in pinky-purple piece of lava

indicators.note: embedded in places the note within the colour

parts.note: puce is a purplish-brown or pinkish-purple colour
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note is lodged in a pink-purple chunk of volcanic rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is light porous rock formed from frothy lava.

clue.text: Bed chamber moustache fertilizer

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot kept under the bed
tash is British slang for a moustache

explanation.surface: A list of odd items: bedroom, chamber, moustache and fertilizer.
explanation.walkthrough: PO is a British word for a chamber pot, and TASH is short for moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound widely used as fertilizer.

clue.text: Reptile of a Brummie's in jail

indicators.note: in tells us the article and the setter's words go inside the jail

parts.note: can is slang for prison
the setter is called Brummie, so Brummie is, said by the setter, becomes I'm

explanation.surface: A reptile belonging to a Brummie is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is called Brummie, so 'Brummie's' (Brummie is) is the setter speaking of themself.
explanation.definitionFit: A caiman is a crocodilian reptile of Central and South America.

clue.text: Forwards actors' business items

definitions.meaning: in rugby the front row forwards include two of these players
objects used on stage by actors

explanation.definitionFit: Props are rugby forwards and also stage properties used by actors.

clue.text: A 6 sat around, in fact, in "flagrante"

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written, fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A symphony sat around and was actually caught in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT and IN FACT are rearranged; 'in flagrante' is the surface's scene. Berlioz's Symphonie fantastique is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlioz's Symphonie fantastique is one of the themed orchestral works.

clue.text: Caveman talk about bad behaviour and taking drugs?

indicators.note: about means the caveman grunt goes round the wrongdoing

parts.note: ug is the grunt of a comic caveman
sin is wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A caveman grunts about bad behaviour and drug-taking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is on drugs is described as using.

clue.text: Callas messed about, reproduced faithfully for a 6

indicators.note: about means the jumbled singer goes round the Latin word
messed means the singer's name is jumbled

parts.note: sic is used to show a quotation is copied exactly as written

explanation.surface: Maria Callas messed about but faithfully reproduced a symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed' makes CLASAL from Callas; 'about' wraps that round SIC. Prokofiev's First Symphony bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev's Symphony No 1 is nicknamed for its imitation of Haydn's style, a themed work.
